title: Canonical finite signed-line and binary scalar comparisons
statement: Fix the finite-coefficient setting [def-pur-conventions], positive levels $1\le m\le n$, the actual fixed-scalar reduction functor Q and the integral-reduced signed coefficient lines, with normalization predicates [def-pur-finite-tensor-reduction-data]. Define the binary strong monoidal structure on Q by the unique structure whose tensorator satisfies the full scalar-first K-flat representative/counit square. Define the signed semilinear line maps by their unique normalized family: quotient on the unit, balancing from the ordinary integral tensor in degree one, ordered tensors on positive powers and evaluation on negative dual powers. For each signed integer r define the derived line comparison Q(A(r)) ≅ B(r) by the unique family whose transpose on single complexes is that actual semilinear map under the specified exact restriction/single comparison. All choices use these uniqueness characterizations, and retain the target B action. The binary representative equation is the explicit square of [def-pur-finite-tensor-comparison-equations]. Tensoring with these line comparisons, preceded by the actual scalar-shift map and inverse binary tensor comparison, gives the canonical natural signed-twist and integer-shift comparison, with components fixed by that explicit formula.

proof.text: Construct the candidate binary structure by the explicit finiteScalarMonoidalModel: the native monoidal total left derived functor of ordinary scalar extension is transported along the canonical uniqueness isomorphism between its adjunction to exact restriction and the chosen fixed scalar adjunction. No monoidal witness is chosen from an unproved existence statement.

Apply finiteScalarMonoidalModel_representative to obtain the full cochain representative/counit square for this particular constructed tensorator. Specializing to K-flat pairs gives the original normalization predicate. The typed finiteScalarTensorData record contains precisely the original source and tail, so projecting it retains the entire square.

Use the proved finiteScalarTensorData_source_isIso API on K-flat pairs. The proved generic existsUnique_core_of_source_tail shows that the candidate square makes the common tail invertible, and cancellation in two normalized squares identifies inverse tensorators. No concrete cochain monoidal data are expanded by this cancellation argument.

Every derived object has a K-flat cochain representative. Tensorator naturality extends equality to every pair. The left unit law, cancellation, whisker exchange and right unitor naturality identify unit maps. Structure extensionality identifies CoreMonoidal. The proved private helpers are core_ext_tensor, core_ext_representatives, existsUnique_core_of_source_tail, cochain_kFlat_density, existsUnique_scalarCore, existsUnique_family, existsUnique_with_family and existsUnique_transposed_lines.

Obtain the uniquely normalized ordinary semilinear signed-line family and the existing pointwise derived comparison theorem. The actual finiteTensorLineComparisonData stores the identical adjunction and transpose values once. Apply the proved generic existsUnique_transposed_lines to its Pointwise and Normalized predicates, then existsUnique_with_family and existsUnique_family assemble the pointwise comparisons with outer ordinary uniqueness. The entire family assembly stays in this module.

Specialize the generic nested-uniqueness assembly to the original ordinary and derived normalization predicates. This proves the original nested ExistsUnique with the same signature and the same ordinary and pointwise derived inputs.

Given that monoidal structure and those line comparisons, use Mathlib Functor.Monoidal.commTensorRight inversely, then tensor the line isomorphism on the right. Whisker the actual scalar-shift isomorphism on the left by tensorRight, compose with this tensor/line isomorphism whiskered on the right by shift, and insert functor associators. Computing the hom component gives exactly finiteTensorTwistShiftComponent, since the induced oplax tensorator is the inverse of the chosen CoreMonoidal tensorator. This argument is proved in the private generic exists_twistShift lemma.

For any other normalized natural isomorphism, the normalization identifies every component with the same prescribed component. Apply Iso.ext, NatTrans.ext and function extensionality to conclude equality. This proves existsUnique_finiteTensorTwistShiftComparison without any new sorry.
